描述_ZN: Scroll of Hibiscus Goose, Ming, Sun Long, on silk, color, 159.3 cm long and 84.1 cm wide.　　The painting is unmarked. Inscriptions: "孫隆圖書", "金川侍御" and "開國忠拇侯孫".　　The picture depicts a large goose looking forward with its head held high, standing sideways under the hibiscus and lake rocks by the grass side of a pond. The hibiscus flowers and leaves are painted with the method of dotting and then outlining, with ink and color interspersed. The Taihu Lake stone is rendered with the boneless method. The goose is both unboned and outlined, with light ink lines outlining the outline and feathers, light ink rendering the flowers, and vermilion brown ochre filling in the muzzle and palm, with a rigid shape and fine brushwork. The whole painting does not stick to the details, but starts from the whole and focuses on the vivid demeanor of the white goose and hibiscus.　　In terms of painting method, the author integrates the painting with the form, the boneless and the outline, the ink and the light color, and harmoniously unifies them in the painting. The origin of this painting method should be the development and variation of the ink and wash painting technique of flowers and birds since Song and Yuan, and it is a creation of Sun Long, which opens up a new style of painting flowers and birds. This painting is his best surviving work.
